quest.title: Detectives
quest.description: Lynette decides to head to the newspaper agency...

talks.objective: Go to the New Fontaine Research Institute
Go and check the suspicious location
Investigate the clues in the base

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Aha, just as we thought — this is where the Imitation Sinthe was being made...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: [Medicine] (Help Chevreuse identify the drugs...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: These bottles and jars... They're all Imitation Sinthe?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...Looks like he's got more than just Imitation Sinthe stashed around here... In addition to the raw materials needed to synthesize the substance itself, there's a large quantity of cleaning agents and a few drugs I haven't been able to identify.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: These cleaning agents are likely used to dispel traces of the substance... like its smell.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: The Special Patrol did some digging into Imitation Sinthe. Our records indicate that it's very difficult for ordinary people to detect traces left behind by this stuff. I'm sure that was the case for Pierre as well.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: It must have taken a considerable amount of time and skill to ensure all those traces get washed away.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: But what are these other drugs for...

talks.objective: Investigate the clues in the base

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: ...When the Marechaussee Phantom searched Pierre's house, there was no sign of these barrels, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He must've moved them. But carrying them all the way out here would attract way too much attention.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: You're right. That doesn't seem like his way of doing things... How did he get them here then?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Examine the barrels...)

dialogues.speaker: Examine Barrels
dialogues.text: (The barrels show signs of water damage. Dried-up water stains can be seen around the circumference of the barrels...)

dialogues.speaker: Examine Barrels
dialogues.text: (There seems to be a pattern to the location of the water stains. For some reason, they appear to be limited to the lower half of the barrels.)

dialogues.speaker: Examine Barrels
dialogues.text: (The lids don't seem very tight, leaving sizeable gaps around the edges. But, there doesn't appear to be any traces of water inside the barrels.)

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Only the lower halves of the barrels appear to have been submerged in water...

talks.objective: Investigate the clues in the base

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The material these bags are made of... It's quite rare...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: [Knowledge] (Help Lyney assess the material...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Doesn't it look similar to the material used for your Magic Pockets?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...It's the very same, actually — Romaritime Flower fiber. But, there's something special about the composition of these bags. I took a closer look, and it appears they're not only waterproof but also corrosion and leak-resistant.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Even the strings look specially designed to keep the bags closed nice and tight.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I came across some bags made of the same material just now, but they were much smaller and thinner. From the look of them, they seemed far less durable as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So... kind of like one of those small, sealed bags?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...Very similar, actually. Normally, it would be easy for a Guard Poodle to sniff out the Imitation Sinthe, but if it was sealed away in a bag like that, it might be possible to elude detection for some time.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But what could these big bags be for then... If the goal is to keep the Imitation Sinthe hidden and sealed away, these bags seem a bit too conspicuous...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Gardemeks ahead!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Look out!

talks.objective: Talk to Lynette and the others
Head underwater and continue searching for clues
Go to your destination to search for clues
Talk to Lynette and the others

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (No... I don't think that can be used to answer the question at hand.)

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Deductive mode deactivated. I think... we may be close to the actual answer.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Why would he leave such an obvious trail for us to follow when he took so much care to not leave any traces of Imitation Sinthe in his home?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: If Bonnie had Imitation Sinthe in her body, then she was a liability that had to be recovered at all costs. But if she wasn't carrying anything, then it would have made sense to tell Bernard not to worry.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: And thinking about it, Bernard only attracted our attention in the first place because he came to look for Bonnie.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Could it be that the person who wrote the letter also knew nothing about Bonnie's whereabouts... or they had a separate goal entirely?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Yeah, according to Bernard, Pierre also supplied all of the goods... But if the Marechaussee Phantom's records are correct, Pierre should have lost all access to the materials required to create the Imitation Sinthe, and the Institute has also not reported any theft of their stocks.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: [Contemplation] Could there be some sort of connection...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: [Animal Handling] I can give it a go... Meow... Meow meow...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lynette could give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Hmm... But maybe I'm overthinking things a bit...)

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: ...Is the answer not coming to you, or do you think it's too unbelievable to be true?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Something on your mind still?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Ah, it was that obvious, huh... Well, even though it didn't feel like Bernard was lying, after talking to him, I'm getting an even stronger sense that something's not quite right.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: We investigated so quickly that perhaps we've missed a thing or two along the way. Let me activate deduction mode and consider things again from the top to see if we can find anything new.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: ...Is there still anything unresolved or strange that we should try to consider?

dialogues.speaker: Chourei
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry, but I can't go with you... Surely, you'll be able to handle him, what between Elodie's Gardemek and all three of you?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Perhaps... we are now closing in on the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About what we found in Poisson...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: The Marechaussee Phantom found Bonnie and the Lefevere pendant at Pierre's residence. That was the beginning point of our investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Bernard's letters...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Bernard claims to have received a letter last night from Pierre. In the letter, Pierre stated that he had gone into hiding. Is there something wrong with the letter...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's an unexplained part in the operations of this trafficking ring...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Well, we've discovered that Bernard is responsible for the trafficking, while Pierre deals with "supplying the goods." Is there something else in this scheme that we're missing?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: The final question is: why did I sense that something wasn't right after hearing Bernard's testimony? Even more so than before...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Perhaps... we are now closing in on the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (No... I don't think that can be used to answer the question at hand.)

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: There's no need to rush. Let's see if we can find any other suspicious points about this case.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Only the lower halves of the barrels appear to have been submerged in water...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: But what are these other drugs for...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But what could these big bags be for then... If the goal is to keep the Imitation Sinthe hidden and sealed away, these bags seem a bit too conspicuous...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I can't believe how much progress we're making with this investigation... Without your help, getting this far would have taken me an awful lot of time and manpower.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: It's rare to see Lynette in serious mode... I wonder how long she'll keep it activated for.
